technical_and_design_decisions: Treat Lattice 0.6.0 as an existing dependency or platform upgrade and preserve the current application architecture unless compatibility requires localized changes.
Replace Spring XD terminology consistently across production code, user interfaces, documentation, examples, tests, configuration, and user-facing messages.
Replace Job and Jobs terminology with Task and Tasks where it refers to the supported domain concept, while preserving unrelated uses of the words.
Reuse existing admin-ui and Flo styling infrastructure, shared assets, and component conventions rather than introducing a new design system.
Display the admin-ui version from the build or package metadata and display the SPI type from the active runtime configuration or backend API.
Implement direct scale-up and scale-down shell commands as Data Flow commands that delegate to the existing platform/SPI scaling operations, including validation and useful error messages.
Use existing test frameworks and integration-test infrastructure for regression coverage, with mock or test SPI implementations where a live deployment is not required.
Capture Flo Graphs as version-controlled documentation images or generated static assets and embed them beside the relevant batch DSL explanations.
assumptions: The existing Lattice repository, build, CI pipeline, admin-ui, Flo, shell, and backend components are available and buildable.
Lattice 0.6.0 has documented upgrade or dependency coordinates; resolving ordinary source and API compatibility issues is included, but a major architectural migration is not.
The increment is implemented by one software developer, and estimates represent active work-hours rather than elapsed calendar time.
The requested terminology changes apply to repository-owned source, tests, documentation, examples, and user-facing text; third-party dependencies and historical migration notes may remain unchanged.
Existing APIs expose sufficient information to obtain the admin-ui version and active SPI type, or require only a small backend endpoint/configuration exposure.

Existing scaling capabilities for module instances are available through the SPI or platform adapter; this increment adds Data Flow shell-level commands rather than implementing a new deployment scaler.
The requested consistent look and feel is a focused visual alignment of shared colors, typography, spacing, navigation, and common components, not a complete UX redesign.
Flo can render the required batch DSL examples using existing graph functionality, and no new graph-rendering engine is required.
Automated tests, documentation updates, and CI/build verification are included; extensive cross-browser, performance, security, or accessibility certification is not.
The specification does not define acceptance-test details, so representative unit, integration, command-line, UI, and documentation checks are used.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the multi-module repository, identify affected backend, shell, admin-ui, Flo, documentation, build, and test areas, establish the current version and terminology baseline, and define the implementation sequence.

Update dependency and project version references, resolve compilation and API compatibility issues, adjust configuration or generated metadata, and verify that the main modules build against Lattice 0.6.0.

Search for and update Spring XD references in Java or other source code, configuration, UI text, documentation, examples, tests, and generated or packaged resources, while checking that no unintended historical references are changed.

activities.activity_name: Replace Job terminology with Task terminology
activities.activity_description: Update domain terminology, labels, command help, documentation, examples, tests, and relevant API-facing strings from Job or Jobs to Task or Tasks, with targeted review for semantic correctness and compatibility-sensitive identifiers.

activities.activity_name: Align admin-ui and Flo visual presentation
activities.activity_description: Review both applications and implement focused consistency changes for shared branding, colors, typography, spacing, navigation, controls, and common visual states; update affected snapshots or UI tests.

activities.activity_name: Add version and SPI type to admin-ui About section
activities.activity_description: Expose or consume build version and active SPI type metadata, update the About view and its styling, handle unavailable or unknown metadata gracefully, and add unit or UI coverage.

activities.activity_name: Add Flo Graph screenshots to batch DSL documentation
activities.activity_description: Create or capture representative Flo Graph images for the documented batch DSL concepts, store them in the documentation assets, embed them at appropriate locations, and verify rendering and references.

Revisit the existing design across the affected components, identify known limitations, inconsistencies, missing tests, API gaps, and upgrade risks, and record actionable findings or issue references alongside the implementation.

activities.activity_name: Implement direct module scaling shell commands
activities.activity_description: Design command syntax and help text, implement scale-up and scale-down commands for a selected module instance, validate arguments and bounds, delegate to the existing SPI or platform operation, format responses, and handle failures consistently.

Add or update unit, command-line, backend integration, UI, terminology, metadata, scaling, and upgrade regression tests; execute representative tests against available mock and integration environments and fix discovered defects.

activities.activity_name: Documentation, release notes, and user guidance
activities.activity_description: Document the new shell commands, version and SPI information, terminology changes, upgrade notes, design limitations, and screenshot-based batch DSL guidance; review examples for consistency.

activities.activity_name: Full build, CI validation, and final cleanup
activities.activity_description: Run the complete build and static checks, validate packaging and generated assets, inspect diffs for stale references, resolve CI failures, perform final cleanup, and prepare the increment for delivery.
